title: Persistent Axis Coverage
prompt:
Implement `AxisCoverageTracker` for permanent coverage on the closed axis `[0, 100]`. Coordinates are expressed in half-unit ticks: tick `t` denotes the real coordinate `t / 2` on the original `[0, 50]` axis.

`ingest(center_twice)` receives an integer center tick and permanently adds the continuous closed interval `[center_twice - 1, center_twice + 1]`, clipped to `[0, 100]`. It returns `True` exactly when the union of every interval seen so far covers the complete continuous axis `[0, 100]`; otherwise it returns `False`. An interval that touches another interval at an endpoint has no gap and must merge. Inputs wholly outside the axis add no coverage. Once the method returns `True`, it must remain `True`.

Store and merge sorted disjoint intervals. Do not rely on floating-point comparisons. A straightforward correct implementation may take O(n) time per ingest for n stored ranges and O(n) state.

example.reasoning: The added tick intervals [0, 2] and [2, 4] touch and merge, but most of the axis remains uncovered.
